samples.summary: The `designEditor` tag omits `verify:doc-index`, a gate a design-editor-only change can fail — violating the change's own stated rule
samples.evidence: The new inert entry claims two claimants (`design-editor:check`, `verify:entropy`) and the design doc states the rule: "enumerate every gate that can currently fail on it, and check each one's route in is a tag rather than `pkgs` or `anyPkg`" (docs/design/harness-engineering.md:456). A third gate qualifies and was not enumerated: `verify:doc-index` (scripts/verify-self.mjs:194) is selected only by `anyPkg: true` + `docsProse`, and `scripts/verify-doc-index.mjs:236-249` fails when `packages/README.md` / `README.md` no longer link into a package directory — `readIndex` drops links whose target no longer exists (line 167). So deleting or renaming `packages/design-editor/README.md` (a change wholly inside `packages/design-editor/**`, which now matches only the inert entry and the `designEditor` tag; `*.md` does not cross a separator so it is not `docsProse`) leaves the package unlinked, `anyPkg` cannot reach the lane for an inert package, and the failure first appears on main's push run — exactly the failure mode this entry was written to avoid. The same gap exists for the pre-existing `documentation` entry, and the new doc table (harness-engineering.md:444-447) records only knip as the differentiator, so it entrenches the incomplete enumeration.

samples.summary: Design doc's base-resolution table under-describes source 2 relative to the shipped code
samples.evidence: The table row says source 2 is `origin/<base.ref>`, but `baseBranchTip` (scripts/changed-areas.mjs:242-250) tries `origin/<ref>`, `upstream/<ref>` and the bare local `<ref>`, each as a remote-tracking ref then as a plain rev. The doc is the canonical record of the resolution order, and the extra sources (particularly the bare local branch, which in a fork checkout can be a stale local `main`) are invisible in it. Also inconsistent with the documented local-fallback rationale a few lines below (scripts/changed-areas.mjs:311-318), which deliberately prefers `upstream` before `origin` for fork checkouts; the new helper reverses that order without saying why.

samples.summary: The `resolveRefs` doc comment is now attached to `mergeRefBaseTip`, leaving the exported function undocumented
samples.evidence: Two JSDoc blocks are stacked at lines 158-216: the first describes `resolveRefs`'s contract (`{ base, head }` or null) but is immediately followed by a second block documenting `mergeRefBaseTip`, so the exported `resolveRefs` at line 252 has no adjacent doc and tooling attributes the first block to nothing. In a file whose comments are the primary design record, this misfiles the contract.

samples.summary: `push` head falls back to the literal `"HEAD"`, contradicting the stated "both ends come from the payload" invariant
samples.evidence: `const head = verified(payload.after) ?? "HEAD"` keeps a checkout-derived end for push events, while the new doc section states the invariant as "Both ends of the diff come from the event payload, and that is load-bearing" (docs/design/harness-engineering.md:466). The push case is lower risk (no merge ref), but the deviation is unexplained in both the code comment and the design doc, so a reader cannot tell whether it is deliberate.

verdict.reason: The finding's mechanism checks out and I found no counterexample. `harness.config.json:40-48` routes `packages/design-editor/**` to tag `designEditor` only; `classify` (scripts/changed-areas.mjs:406-418) short-circuits the packages/ classification for an inert match so `packages` is empty (asserted by scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs:755-768). `verify:doc-index` (scripts/verify-self.mjs:194-199) is selected only by `anyPkg` + `docsProse`, is not a `needs` target of any lane, and the repo's own lane test (scripts/test/verify-self-lanes.test.mjs:164-186) confirms a designEditor-tagged change selects only `design-editor:check` and `verify:entropy`. The gate is genuinely failable by a design-editor-only change: both indexes link into the package through a file (packages/README.md:34, README.md:75), readIndex drops dead links (scripts/verify-doc-index.mjs:161-169) and collectFindings then reports the package as unlinked and exits 1 (scripts/verify-doc-index.mjs:236-249, 291-300). No other gate covers it — verify-entropy reads only docs/design (scripts/verify-entropy.mjs:212-266, 462-465) and harness-engineering.md:228-230 itself says doc-index is "the only dead-link check the package and script indexes get". So the entry's own stated rule at docs/design/harness-engineering.md:455-457 ("enumerate every gate that can currently fail on it") is not satisfied, and the doc table at 444-447 records only knip as the second claimant. The only mitigation I found is .githooks/pre-commit:20 running `pnpm verify:fast` (which includes verify:doc-index, package.json:12) — a bypassable local hook, not the CI merge gate the rule is about, so it does not refute the finding.
